gaps.term: nodes, edges and routes of the network
gaps.quote: Along an edge from node $\alpha$ to node $\beta$ the stored array changes by $D_\beta D_\alpha^{-1}$.
gaps.note: The page never says what the nodes are in the wiring (sources, gates, sinks on a wire), what an edge is (it joins consecutive nodes on one wire; the paper defines this at line 665-690) or what a route is. The reader has only 'fixed wiring of linear steps' and cannot tell what is being composed.

gaps.term: route from input role w to output role rho(w)
gaps.quote: Take an input role $w$ and its route to output role $\rho(w)$
gaps.note: Edges stay on one wire, so a chain of edges ends at the same role it started from; reaching a different role rho(w) goes through gates that mix wires. The page does not say how a route crosses gates, nor that the input array is the stored array at the source (the paper, lines 141-144 and 795-810, defines the logical input as the inverse source frame applied to the physical input, and obtains the endpoint operator from the whole-network identity D_out S D_in^{-1} at line 816, not from composing edge operators alone). The page's telescoping of edge operators therefore does not by itself justify the route operator.

gaps.quote: arrays indexed by the common address set
gaps.note: The page never defines the common address set (the paper, line 127, says all role streams have the same local address set), nor says that all roles' arrays are indexed by it, which the pointwise gates and the single frame D_nu rely on.

gaps.quote: The frame $D_\nu$ of the gate is linear and the coefficients are scalars, so
gaps.note: The identity needs the frame to be linear over the scalar ring (the paper says R-linear, line 811) and every one of the p inputs to be in that same frame D_nu, since all incidences of one gate share its frame (paper line 135). The page gives only linearity and does not say the inputs arrive in the gate's frame.

gaps.quote: if a route has source frame $I$ and sink frame $D_\nu$, its operator is $D_\nu$, however many gates it passes through.
gaps.note: By the page's own formula the route applies epsilon_w D_sink D_source^{-1}, which is -D_nu when epsilon_w = -1. The operator is D_nu only for sign +1 or after the sign has been undone, as the page says two paragraphs earlier. The paper (lines 818-822) keeps the sign in the route operator.
